chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Jameela Al-Basri who said:

I was with Yunus in Baghdad, and while I was walking with him in the market, the owner of the fermented drink opened his container, and it splashed onto Yunus's garment. I saw him become distressed by this until the sun set. I said to him, 'Will you not pray, O Abu Muhammad?' He said, 'I do not wish to pray until I return home and wash this wine from my garment.' I said to him, 'Is this your own opinion or a report you are conveying?' He said, 'Hisham ibn al-Hakam informed me that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fermented drink, and he (peace be upon him) said: Do not drink it, for it is an unknown wine. So if it touches your garment, wash it.'

key_terms.أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad; an epithet for Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, a prominent companion of the Imams.
key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: Fermented drink (specifically beer or ale), distinct from grape wine.
key_terms.خَمْرٌ مَجْهُولٌ: Unknown wine; a technical term indicating a drink that is wine but its intoxicating nature or specific type is not definitively known, affecting purity rulings.
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: So wash it; the prescribed action for removing the substance from the garment.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing garments splashed with fermented drinks like beer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the jurisprudential distinction between *khamr majhool* (unknown wine) and other impurities, illustrating the practical application of Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling to Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman. It underscores the Shia principle that fermented beverages not explicitly identified as intoxicating in their current state do not render garments *najis* (impure) upon contact, requiring only simple washing rather than full ablution or ritual bath. This reflects the broader scholarly consensus on the conditional nature of wine's impurity based on its intoxicating effect and identification.
